content.text: The brigands exploit Mugsborough through corrupt council decisions, inflated contracts, low wages, and unsafe, shoddy work. At “The Cave,” they discuss council schemes and indulge in ignorant pseudo-science; at the Town Council, they approve profiteering deals while cutting workers’ wages. Unemployment, poverty, apathy, and hostility to Owen’s Socialism dominate working-class life. The men endure exhausting, dangerous labour for Rushton, whose firm cheats customers and steals materials. Their Beano travels from the Cricketers to the Queen Elizabeth at Tubberton, exposing class servility and political division. Barrington later delivers a Socialist oration at “The Refuge,” advocating public ownership and organized industry. Soon afterward, Philpot is crushed by a defective “Sixty-five” ladder at The Refuge. His body is taken to the mortuary, but rival undertakers compete for the funeral. Rushton’s men eventually carry a coffin to Philpot’s house and begin transferring his corpse into their cheaper coffin.
